title: Corn Tortillas (Gluten-Free)
description: Traditional corn tortillas are made from nixtamalized masa harina, producing a naturally gluten-free tortilla with authentic corn flavor and a soft, tender texture. Freshly cooked tortillas are perfect for tacos, tostadas, enchiladas, and countless Mexican dishes.

ingredients.title: Ingredients
items: Masa harina (high-quality, nixtamalized corn flour – e.g., Masienda or Maseca) – 2 cups (240 g)
Neutral oil (like avocado or sunflower) – 1 tsp (optional, for added pliability)

ingredients.title: Equipment
items: Tortilla press (lined with plastic or cut freezer bag)

instruction.title: Step 1 – Mix the Dough (Masa)
steps: In a large bowl, combine masa harina and salt.
Slowly add warm water, mixing with your hand until a soft, pliable dough forms.
The dough should feel like playdough — moist but not sticky.
If too dry, add 1 tsp water at a time. If too wet, sprinkle in a little more masa harina.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Rest
steps: Cover the dough with a damp towel and let it rest for 20–30 minutes at room temperature.
This allows the masa to fully hydrate, improving texture.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Portion
steps: Divide dough into 12–15 golf ball-sized pieces (about 30 g each).
Keep them covered with a damp towel to prevent drying.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Press
steps: Place one dough ball between sheets of plastic in the tortilla press.
Press firmly to form a 5–6 inch (12–15 cm) tortilla, about 2 mm thick.

instruction.title: Step 5 – Cook (Professional Technique)
steps: Heat a cast-iron comal or heavy skillet over medium-high until very hot.
Place tortilla on the dry comal.
First side: 40–50 seconds until edges begin to release.
Third flip: 20–30 seconds — the tortilla should puff slightly (a sign of perfect hydration and pressing).
Adjust timing depending on heat; tortillas should develop light brown spots but not burn.

instruction.title: Step 6 – Hold & Serve
steps: Stack tortillas in a clean kitchen towel to keep warm and pliable.
Serve within 30 minutes for best texture, or store wrapped in a towel inside a tortilla warmer.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Perfect for tacos, tostadas, enchiladas, and quesadillas.
Pair with tacos al pastor, carnitas, grilled vegetables, or mole-based dishes.
Serve warm straight from the comal for the best flavor and texture.

chefTips: Hydration is key: Different masa harina brands absorb water differently; always adjust slightly.
Puffing: Indicates steam expansion — essential for tenderness. If tortillas don’t puff, knead dough more or adjust hydration.
Make ahead: Tortillas can be reheated on a comal for 10–15 seconds per side.
Pairing: Ideal for tacos al pastor, carnitas, grilled vegetables, or mole-based dishes.
